openFindings.title: A containment pass whose quarantine evidence failed to write is indistinguishable from a complete one
openFindings.evidence: enforceWriteContainment returns the full QuarantineResult {dirPath, entries, refused, error} (write-containment.ts:1331-1354), but buildContainmentViolationEvent carries only violations, reverted, the patch path and dataLossPossible; the runner appends that event (fanout-run.cjs:3526-3544) and keeps only quarantinePath for output.containment (:3649-3652), dropping refused and error. For a lane that fails a gate, even quarantinePath is discarded with the thrown error (:3585-3626). A pass whose manifest failed, or whose destinations the phase-008 canonicality check refused, therefore reads exactly like a complete pass wherever the violation is reported.
openFindings.recommendation: Carry {dirPath, refused, error} on the containment event (or on output.containment for failed lanes too) so an incomplete quarantine record is visible next to the violation it belongs to.
openFindings.scopeProof: Read the enforce return contract, the event builder, and both runner consumers (successful and failed lane paths); grepped the event type for quarantine fields (none).

openFindings.title: Residual worktree claims remain in the summary, tasks and handover records
openFindings.evidence: Implementation-summary presents worktrees and the isolation tally as shipped in the frontmatter description (:3), files table (:67), verification narrative (:75), key decisions (:87-88) and verification rows (:98-106) against the single removal paragraph at :61. tasks.md:88 is a checked task whose evidence names the deleted worktree-lifecycle and worktree-lease suites. handover.md:100 sends a cold reader to ADR-004 for the worktree-default decision without naming ADR-007, though :37 was corrected.
openFindings.recommendation: Mark the worktree claims in the summary and task evidence superseded or remove them, and correct the handover's cold-read order to ADR-007.
openFindings.scopeProof: Read each file's worktree mentions in context and cross-checked against the phase-007 removal and ADR-007.

openFindings.title: The closure gate is still In Progress and its Met rows cite deleted or shifted evidence
openFindings.evidence: Status In Progress dated 2026-09-08 (:50-51). AC-015 is Met citing runtime/tests/unit/worktree-lifecycle.vitest.ts:531/:547, a file phase 007 deleted; AC-018 (:80) is Met citing runtime/tests/unit/fanout-run.vitest.ts:4184/:4212/:4228, but that file grew from 4374 to 4791 lines in the remediation and those lines are unrelated scaffolding (4184 a spawn-argument list, 4212 an opencode --variant test, 4228 closing braces). The closure statement (:107) reads closeable and awaiting sign-off. Prior F-010 class; AC-009/AC-017 were superseded but the gate was never re-anchored or re-dated.
openFindings.recommendation: Re-anchor or supersede the two Met rows, mark AC-015 Superseded by ADR-007 like AC-009/AC-017, and re-date the metadata against HEAD.
openFindings.scopeProof: Verified the deleted suite by directory listing; read every cited line at HEAD; wc -l on the test file; checked for a newer AC file in the packet tree (none).

claimAdjudication.claim: The packet's closure gate carries a non-terminal status and certifies two Met criteria with evidence that no longer resolves to the behaviour it names.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Listed the unit test directory to prove the worktree suite is gone; read the cited lines at HEAD; checked the AC file's history and the prior registry's F-010 entry.
claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: The gate's own metadata says In Progress, which is honest; but the row-level Met assertions are evidence claims that no longer hold, and the packet's completion criterion depends on the gate being actionable.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to P2 if the rows are re-anchored or the file is marked historical by the operator; upgrade if a release decision is taken from the gate as written.

openFindings.title: The empty-hash sentinel still hides a baseline path the lane recreates
openFindings.evidence: detectNewOutOfScopeViolations skips every baseline path whose recorded hash is empty (`const preHash = preMap.get(p) || ''; if (!preHash) continue;`). The snapshot stores hash:'' for any path git hash-object cannot read, including a tracked path deleted before dispatch, because gitHashObject returns '' on a non-zero exit (write-containment.ts:506-510). The phase-009 addition (:930-953) walks the subtraction the other way only for entries marked untracked whose path is absent from status AND absent from disk (:936-938, :944), so a lane that recreates the path is excluded by construction. The only test pins the subtraction case (tests/unit/write-containment.vitest.ts:535-554); no case covers recreation.
openFindings.recommendation: Give unhashable-but-recorded baseline paths a distinct absent state and re-evaluate them with the content-identity check when they reappear, instead of storing '' and treating it as unmatched forever.
openFindings.scopeProof: Read the full detection path, the snapshot writer and gitHashObject; read the phase-009 deletion tests and grepped for a recreation case (none).

openFindings.title: The opt-in restore still writes through a symlinked ancestor directory
openFindings.evidence: Phase 011's lstat guard inspects only the final component (:1433-1434). Both baseline write arms then join the repo-relative path and write along it: mkdirSync(dirname(...)) + writeFileSync at :1447-1449 and :1493-1494. A lane that replaces a parent directory of the violated path with a symlink to a directory outside the checkout redirects the write; the link node itself is preserved by the not-in-HEAD branch (:1480-1481). canonicalPath/isSubpath (:616-677) already implement the every-component rule detection uses (:669-677); the write path does not call it.
openFindings.recommendation: Canonicalize the destination through every component (reuse canonicalPath) and refuse when it leaves the worktree, or refuse any violated path whose parent chain contains a symlink.
openFindings.scopeProof: Read both baseline write arms in full, the not-in-HEAD preservation branch, the quarantine refusal (artifact-side only), and the detection canonicalization for comparison; no git write experiment was run, so the HEAD branch is recorded as unverified rather than claimed.

claimAdjudication.claim: Under opt-in restore, a violated path whose parent directory the lane replaced with a symlink is written through that link, so captured baseline bytes land wherever the link points, possibly outside the repository.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Read the whole revert function for an ancestor canonicalization (none); checked whether the symlink node is removed first (preserved, :1480-1481); checked whether quarantine's refusal covers the repo-side write (artifact-side only); no git checkout experiment (banned for this lineage).
claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: The lane must plant the symlink itself and that write is a reported violation; under preserve nothing is written. The damage is reachable only under the restore opt-in, whose post-phase-011 contract is that a restore never writes through a symlink.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to P2 if a caller canonicalizes join(repoRoot, violation.path) before revertOutOfScopeViolations (none found), or if restore mode is unreachable from the shipped command surface (it is wired through fanout-run.cjs).

openFindings.title: The remediation did not sweep the caller envelope's duplication and diagnostics residue
openFindings.evidence: Ten byte-identical inline containment call blocks remain: deep-research-auto.yaml 4, deep-research-confirm.yaml 1, deep-review-auto.yaml 4 (:1521, :1615, :1705, :1795), deep-review-confirm.yaml 1. drainGitContentionWarnings is exported from write-containment.ts:393 and drained at exactly one site, fanout-run.cjs:3323, so an exhausted retry budget in an inline iteration is recorded and discarded. Prior F-019/F-020, unbound to any remediation phase.
openFindings.recommendation: Extract one shared helper for the call envelope, and drain or log the contention warnings where they are produced.
openFindings.scopeProof: Counted the call blocks per file by grep; grepped every drainGitContentionWarnings reference (export, tests, one call site).

openFindings.title: The restore writer addresses violation paths against a repo root that may be a subdirectory
openFindings.evidence: resolveContainmentRepoRoot returns cwd unless the artifact tree lives in a different worktree, while git status paths are worktree-root-relative regardless of -C. The write arms join those paths against opts.repoRoot (write-containment.ts:1449, :1494); the deletion pass's disk check correctly uses scope.repoRealRoot (:944). Latent for shipped callers (all dispatch with working_directory: repo_root), re-registered because the remediation put this path on a write surface. Prior F-004, still active.
openFindings.recommendation: Resolve the guard root to the git toplevel (the helper already has gitToplevel) or assert that cwd is the toplevel before containment runs.
openFindings.scopeProof: Read the resolver, its only caller in fanout-run, and both write arms; confirmed the deletion pass uses the resolved scope root while the write arms do not.

openFindings.title: The spec still mandates the worktree mechanism it removed, in every section except the two requirement rows
openFindings.evidence: Frontmatter description (:3), trigger phrase (:8), executive summary (:22), key decisions (:24), critical dependencies (:26), purpose (:57), files table (:85-89), SC-003 (:162), SC-005 (:164), NFR-R02 (:207), failure modes (:220-221) and risks (:245-246) all present per-lineage worktrees as shipped; the packet reads Status Complete (:36) and phase 007 (ca713e3478) deleted the mechanism and its suites. Only REQ-005 (:140) and REQ-007 (:148) carry supersession markers, while the remediation record claims the parent-doc findings were fixed directly (goal.md:119).
openFindings.recommendation: Mark SC-003/SC-005/NFR-R02 Superseded by ADR-007 as the requirement rows already are, and rewrite the frontmatter, executive summary, purpose, dependency, failure-mode and risk text to the shared-checkout design.
openFindings.scopeProof: Grepped every worktree occurrence in the file (31 hits) and checked each for a supersession marker; checked for a global historical note (none); cross-checked ADR-007, the phase-007 commit and the AC file.

claimAdjudication.claim: The parent spec still presents per-lineage worktrees as shipped in its framing, success criteria, non-functional requirements, failure modes and risks, contradicting the tree phase 007 shipped and the packet's Complete status.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Grepped all worktree mentions and their markers; looked for a global historical note above the sections (none); verified ADR-007 declares removal and AC marks the two worktree rows superseded.
claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: The requirement table is normative and marked, so no reader would rebuild worktrees from §4; the frontmatter and executive summary, however, are the packet's abstract, and two unmarked success criteria can never pass.
